correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western headward ravine
correspondence.finding: The first selected reach follows a recognizable southeastward ravine cut through the western hills, with converging minor washes, into the headward alluvial depression. Small clouds lie around this terrain, but the chosen ravine and its receiving valley are visible. No local stream name is supplied.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper small-pan complex and southward transfer
correspondence.finding: The selection enters a broad pale alluvial/pan floor, bends east and south beside an elongated water-filled depression, then turns toward a separate southern collector. The images show these landforms and several local wash traces, but do not establish the whole selected inter-pan passage and onward southward transfer as one connected channel. This is a substantive connection gap rather than a missing name or an exact-bank mismatch.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern collector and southeastward valley
correspondence.finding: From the southern wash junction, the selected route follows an observable pale incised drainage southeastward between low ridges. Its several bends and arrival at the larger eastward corridor are visible; this downstream correspondence does not resolve the preceding inter-pan transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle valley, northward dogleg and southern loop
correspondence.finding: The selected middle bends, northward dogleg, eastward passage and broad southern loop lie within the same observable incised alluvial corridor. Joining ravines and the return northeastward are recognizable at ordinary corridor scale. Isolated small cloud shadows and generalized bend placement do not create another material gap. No selected reservoir, glacier or managed passage is established here.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower braided/alluvial approach to the receiving basin
correspondence.finding: The lower west-to-east wash broadens into a pale braided/alluvial floor, passes north of the separate small southern pond and turns northeast into the main receiving basin. The lower joins and basin entry are geographically supported; adjacent ponds are not silently treated as named river reaches.

correspondence.component_scope: Receiving lake/playa interior and actual selected ending
correspondence.finding: The final selected northward continuation and short westward ending lie within the broad receiving lake/playa floor. Geographic entry and receiving-setting correspondence are complete. No river line across the lake floor, contemporary water level, or through-flow to another basin is required or asserted. The report identifies this western project-margin lake as Laguna Salada, also Lago Gran Laguna Salada.

correspondence.component_scope: Westernmost pond/wetland feeder and first lake entry
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in an upland mosaic of narrow ponds, wet ground and rocky/vegetated terrain. Some dark-water segments and the receiving lake are visible, but the entire small southeastward feeder and its final entry are insufficiently exposed to establish a continuous selected through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: First large lake passage and northward outlet chain
correspondence.finding: The selection continues across the eastern side of the first larger lake, turns north and then northeast through a visible constricted chain of open water and channel. The lake passage and its northern exit correspond at ordinary regional scale. Individual waterbody names are not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper elongated lake and eastward stream/lake succession
correspondence.finding: The northeastern outlet leads through a sinuous connecting corridor into an elongated east-west waterbody and then successive narrow eastward water/channel reaches. The image shows the selected sequence and joins; generalized lake-centerline placement is not treated as a shoreline or name-boundary claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Long middle lake and south-turning outlet
correspondence.finding: The middle image exposes the long narrow waterbody, its eastern outlet, the channel across the pale sandy/rocky margin and the pronounced southward bend into the lower tributary valley. All intervening stored part joins lie within this visible connected corridor. Peters River and Lindo Lake are not spatially assigned from an unlocated name list.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward southern tributary and confluence
correspondence.finding: A narrow meandering watercourse continues east through the vegetated and wetland-fringed valley and visibly joins the broader river approaching from the northwest. This correspondence keeps the southern tributary separate from the receiving river; its local name remains unassigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Receiving Goose River lower meanders
correspondence.finding: After the confluence, the selection follows the wider river east and northeast toward the settled lower valley. The official2022 road-works account identifies Goose River Bridge on Route520; the independently authored2019 paddle account uses Goose River at the adjacent lake shore. These support the receiving identity, together with the visible lower corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Bridge, delta passage and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The eastern image shows the road crossing, downstream meanders, sandy mouth channel and receiving inner bay. The selected endpoint reaches that mouth corridor rather than ending at the upstream confluence or bridge. Adjacent side channels and bay-margin wetlands do not require an exact present-day tidal shoreline assignment.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern headward opening
correspondence.finding: The selected opening south of Cuanajo follows the northward tributary shown in the eastern Pátzcuaro relief map and basin map. It crosses into Huiramba through the same branching corridor. The short opening has no separately established name.

correspondence.component_scope: Canacucho and Huiramba–Lagunillas feeder
correspondence.finding: Huiramba relief mapping follows the selected western tributary into the reach labelled Canacucho, then the northeastern continuation labelled Tupatarol. The adjoining El Pedregal tributary remains separate. The basin map supplies the continuation past Huiramba toward Lagunillas.

correspondence.component_scope: Lagunillas bend and Tupátaro approach
correspondence.finding: The selected eastward bend south of Lagunillas and continuing approach toward Tiripetío correspond to connected source linework. Morelia relief mapping labels this upper corridor Tupátaro. The Huiramba spelling Tupatarol is preserved as a source-specific label rather than silently imposed throughout.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper junction and Cointzio reservoir passage
correspondence.finding: The selected northeastern tributary meets the separately mapped southeastern approach and enters Cointzio at its southwestern arm. The waterbody and northern outlet align with the continuing channel toward Morelia. The reservoir retains its own identity.

correspondence.component_scope: Grande de Morelia through the city
correspondence.finding: Morelia relief mapping directly labels Grande de Morelia along the selected northward and then eastward city corridor. It depicts the continuing channel and the joining Chiquito drainage separately; Chiquito is not the selected headward feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Charo corridor and lower northward turn
correspondence.finding: The basin map follows the selected southern, meandering corridor past Charo and its lower junction into the northward channel beside Álvaro Obregón. Parallel northern drainage and irrigation lines are distinguished from this selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower straightened channel and lake entry
correspondence.finding: Álvaro Obregón relief mapping depicts the selected long, straightened northward channel and its northeastern bend into the eastern lake margin. Viejo de Morelia is labelled on a separate western route and is not assigned to this selected channel. The local lower-channel name is left unset.

correspondence.component_scope: Receiving lake and actual rendered ending
correspondence.finding: The mapped entry leads into Lago de Cuitzeo. The final westward and northwestern display continuation ends within that same receiving waterbody. Lake-entry and terminal-setting correspondence are complete; the lake interior is not asserted to be a separately named river channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and northeastward upper passage
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening lies in the original's ice-covered terrain among small exposed-rock projections and elongated rock bodies south of the Geikie Plateau label. The initial northeastward turn and all six stored parts are covered in the continuous original view. Ice contours and geological boundaries are not interpreted as river channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward upper corridor and northernmost arc
correspondence.finding: The selection continues east through the mapped ice/exposed-rock mosaic and reaches its northernmost arc beside successive elongated rock bodies. Every intervening stored join is covered. The original establishes the regional terrain sequence without supplying a natural-river name for it.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward middle turn
correspondence.finding: The southeastward turn and short intermediate parts pass through the same continuously depicted mixed ice and exposed-rock setting. The source covers the whole turn and its entry and exit joins; no lake, reservoir or managed-channel identity is established for these parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward lower connector and final southward turn
correspondence.finding: The selected eastward connector, its slight northward bend and the ensuing turn toward the coast are geographically accounted for among the original's rock-bounded ice passages. Both sides of each internal join are in the inspected map area. No named river through-link is inferred from neighboring geographic labels.

correspondence.component_scope: Long southward coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The long southward component runs through the original's narrow ice/exposed-rock belt between elongated coastal rock bodies. Its full length, bends and join to the final stored part were read in the continuous selected-corridor view and enlarged terminal setting. This is terrain correspondence, not evidence of surface or subglacial hydraulic continuity.

correspondence.component_scope: Final part and actual selected ending
correspondence.finding: The final southward part and all of its bends remain covered through the narrow historical ice/rock coastal passage. The actual selected ending is at the mapped ice-front/coastal-water transition between exposed-rock headlands, with the receiving coastal-water setting visible beyond it. No exact glacier or fjord name is assigned. The modeled sea class does not independently establish a surveyed river mouth or present-day ice-front position.
